subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw make CLI health/status/stability RPC-first with no file-level WAL maintenance while a gateway owns the shared DB, or enforce a broader single-writer lease for all non-gateway shared-state openers?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the permanent fix changes CLI observability, doctor/migration behavior, gateway ownership, and corruption recovery policy for a P0 persisted-state surface.

options.title: RPC-first, no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Make health/status/stability use the running gateway when available and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway owner is active.

options.title: Single-writer lease
options.body: Have the gateway own write and WAL-maintenance access through an explicit lease, with every other process refusing writer-style shared-state DB opens while it is held.

options.title: Recovery first
options.body: Land preserve/quarantine/fresh-state recovery for malformed openclaw.sqlite first, then separately address concurrent CLI/gateway maintenance prevention.

recommendation.title: RPC-first, no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Make health/status/stability use the running gateway when available and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway owner is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal ties this shared SQLite ownership contract to the database-first refactor and plugin-state migration.
